title: Rate/Queue Admission Guardrails for Dedicated Pools: token-bucket + shedding lanes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a production-grade admission control and dedicated routing layer for Dedicated capacity pools that enforces throughput guarantees while preventing overload. This ticket specifies the token-bucket rate-limiter, configurable priority lanes with queueing timeouts, and overload-shedding policies that prefer graceful degradation (fallback model/region) over hard failures.
problem_statement: Dedicated pools currently accept traffic until CUDA OOMs or tail-latency spikes cause large numbers of 5xx errors. We need admission controls that (1) enforce committed throughput per-customer/pool, (2) allow controlled bursting, (3) provide prioritized request handling for critical routes, and (4) shed excess load predictably to preserve SLOs for committed customers.
proposed_solution: Per-pool token-bucket admission with configurable refill rates and burst sizes tied to committed throughput in reserve contracts.
Priority lanes: design three lanes (critical, standard, best-effort). Lanes have independent queue size and enqueue TTL. Requests promoted/demoted based on route metadata and route-level SLAs.
Queueing: in-memory prioritized queues with admission FIFO within lane, time-based dequeue decision; configurable max_wait_ms; if timeout, trigger shedding or fallback policy.

Overload shedding: configurable policies per pool: reject (429), route to fallback model (cheaper/quantized), route to different region/dedicated tier, or enqueue to limited overflow store with async processing.
Backpressure signals: expose token-bucket headroom and queue depth via runtime metrics and a light-weight HTTP endpoint for agents to adapt client retry/backoff logic.
Graceful fallback path: when shedding chosen, prefer model-variant fallback with deterministic quality downgrade and annotate responses with structured metadata explaining the reason.
Control plane UI: Console support to edit admission configs per-pool, visualize queue depth, historical shedding events and cost impact.
Compatibility: admission logic pluggable with existing request router; default policy should be safe for older clients (reject fast instead of blocking indefinitely).
acceptance_criteria: Config schema documented and accepted by PM/Console team
Per-pool token-bucket enforcement implemented and unit-tested
Priority lanes implemented with queue TTL and per-lane size limit
Overload shedding policy supports at least 3 actions: reject, fallback_model, and region_redirect
Metrics emitted: bucket_tokens, queue_depth{lane}, shed_events{policy}, enqueue_latency_percentiles
E2E test harness shows 95th p99 latency preserved for critical lane under 3x committed load by shedding best-effort traffic
Console shows live queue depth and a historical chart for shed_events
Runbook updated with steps to change policies and emergency disable admission control

2026-03-10 - Tomas: Implemented lane-based queues with TTL eviction. Discovered GC pressure when queue kept references to large request objects; switching to lightweight descriptors. Patch in flight: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3265

2026-03-12 - Engineering sync: Agreed on default policy: token-bucket strict for committed throughput, short queues for critical lane (max wait 50ms), standard lane max wait 200ms, best-effort max wait 1000ms, then shed-by-fallback model. Documented in design doc link below.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive shedding protects committed customers but may surprise self-serve users. Console needs clear UX and default soft-limits for new customers.
We considered centralized admission (single global controller) vs in-node local enforcement. Chosen: hybrid: local fast-path token check, periodic sync with control-plane for quota changes.
Open question: should we charge for queued time or API tokens consumed during queue; PM recommends no charge for queued waiting time for now.
Performance note: token-bucket check must remain lock-free on hot path; use per-shard counters and atomic ops.
Fallback models must be explicitly listed in model-catalog to avoid returning unsupported artifacts. ENG-11750 is dependency.
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket edge cases (burst drain, refill under load)
Integration test: simulate stripe of 5x committed load, assert shed_events increase and critical-lane SLOs preserved
Chaos experiment: kill 20% of serving replicas under load and verify shedding behaves deterministically
Load test with Prometheus alerts enabled to ensure metrics emitted under high-throughput scenarios
Canary rollout: enable policy on single pool for 48h, monitor shed_events and customer errors before wide rollout
